| wl-0009 | Calculated columns and rows — derived tallies, recomputed on edit | A total typed into a table is a claim that goes stale the moment any row it summarises changes, and nothing detects it — precisely the class plan 001 spent four phases cataloguing: a figure that was true when written. dd already renders .dd.md deterministically from .dd.json, so a tally computed at build time CANNOT rot: it is derived, never asserted, and `dd build --check` already fails on drift. This turns a whole category of stale-number defect into an impossibility rather than a discipline. | idea | m | shape not settled — see the open questions in the note | Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: "next wishlist item is calculated columns (auto gens the total on edits, ato adds total column at bottom. cal tally cols and rows with setting." | AS ASKED: totals regenerate on edit (any set/add/rm touching a tallied section), a total row is appended automatically, and both column and row tallies are configurable by a setting. OPEN SHAPE QUESTIONS, recorded rather than guessed: (1) does the setting live in the SCHEMA — a field declares itself summable, so every document of that type tallies alike — or in the DOCUMENT, per-instance? Schema-side is more deterministic and matches how dd resolves everything else; document-side is more flexible. (2) Which aggregates: sum only, or count/min/max/mean? (3) Do tallies MATERIALISE into the .dd.json, or exist only in the rendered .dd.md? Render-only keeps the source a single truth and avoids write amplification on every edit, which argues strongly for it — and it is the option that makes the total underivable-from-anything-but-the-data. (4) What happens to a non-numeric or empty cell in a tallied column — skip, zero, or refuse? Refusing fits this repo: a silently-skipped cell produces a wrong total that looks right, which is the exact failure mode the feature exists to remove. |
| wl-0010 | Custom validation — semantic rules as portable, declarable data rather than dd code | Today dd validates STRUCTURE (does this field match the schema shape) while the SEMANTIC rules — a plan must have acceptance criteria, an AC must link to a task, a task's state derives from its assertions — live as hard-coded TypeScript in services/dd/plan. That means only we can express a semantic rule, only for the document families we shipped, and every new discipline needs a code change and a release. Making the rules declarable turns dd from 'a validator that knows about builder plans' into 'a validator anyone can teach', and lets a team encode its own conventions without forking us. | shaped | xl | wl-0001 — this is an SDK-surface decision and should be designed inside that flow, not ahead of it | Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: "i want the rules that we usein pln to be expressable via a portable and customisable validation concept somehow so anyone can implement semantic validation across the top (plans must have acs, acs mst link to tasks in this file) etc. This will rely heavily on the typing system (ac must have at least one link to typeof tasks.dd/tasklist or what ever)." Raised in the same breath as his note on OQ-2 — "ah yes, but later we will remove" — which is the strategic point below. | THIS IS THE THING THAT MAKES services/dd/plan REMOVABLE, which is why Jordan raised it while answering OQ-2. Whatever we decide about shipping plan/ publicly is a TRANSITIONAL answer: once semantic rules are declarable, the hard-coded plan semantics become a set of rules attached to the builder/plan schema, and the module carrying them stops needing to exist as a public export. Decide OQ-2 for today's consumer, not for all time. IT LEANS ON THE TYPE SYSTEM, which dd already has and which is the real asset here: links are already rel-typed and target-typed (a proven_by must point at builder/execution-log/section/entries, and E406 link-type-mismatch already fires when it does not). Jordan's example — an AC must carry at least one link of type X to a document of type Y — is a CARDINALITY constraint over an existing typed edge, not a new concept. That is a strong sign the rule vocabulary can be small. SHAPE QUESTIONS for the design flow, recorded not guessed: (1) where do rules live — beside the schema (travelling with the family, so any repo resolving that schema inherits its rules) or in the consuming repo (local conventions over a shared family)? Both are wanted; the resolution order matters more than either. (2) How expressive: declarative predicates over the typed graph (cardinality, required-link-of-type, cross-document reachability) or an escape hatch to real code? A jiti-loaded custom type already exists as precedent for the escape hatch. (3) Are violations errors, warnings, or severity-declared by the rule? The plan validator already distinguishes ERROR from contradiction-class WARN, so severity is already a live concept. (4) NON-VACUITY: a rule engine can silently match nothing. Every rule needs to be provably capable of firing — the same requirement this repo puts on its own guards, and the reason plan 001 found a pin whose docstring claimed more than it pinned. |
